pr_title: resolved: if one transaction completes, expect other transactions within candidate to succeed quickly
pr_body:
Intended to address https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/22575 Some earlier discussion here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/35514

This implements point 1 from Poetterings suggestion here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/35514#issuecomment-2537373998

I do not think point 2 in that comment makes sense to implement right now, because for broken DNS servers (and the whole point of this change is to work around broken DNS servers), one possible behavior we are seeing is that for some domains, we get A and AAAA responses, while for other domains we only get an A response and never get an AAAA response. So depending on what domains we've queried earlier, we could see both many successful AAAA transactions and many timed-out AAAA transactions, without this giving us any indication if a given future AAAA transaction will succeed or timeout.

Fixes: #22575
pr_comments: looks conceptually good, just some tweaks please.
Thanks for the feedback! Pushed commits which should have addressed all the comments.
lgtm, except for SD_ prefix thing, see above.
@mhs-emlogic Could you extend the commit message? At least, summarize the suggestion by Lennart in #35514, mention that this fixes #22575.

comments:
Seems your DNS server doesn't answer at all if asked for IPV6 addresses? i.e. AAAA?

Client program sends a request to resolve both IPv4 and IPv6 address of `sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com`. The A lookup works from cache in the excerpt you posted, the AAAA lookup times out after we keep repeating the lookup.

If you use add `-t aaaa` to your `host` invocations, does that work or also hang?

If you add `-4` to your `resolvectl query` invocations, does that complete quickly?

I will test this in the failing env when I'm there next, in a week or so.  In the meantime, here is the output in a working env:

[jlquinn@tiamat seminar]$ time resolvectl query -i wlp4s0 -4 sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com
sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com: 129.42.49.10           -- link: wlp4s0

-- Information acquired via protocol DNS in 770us.
-- Data is authenticated: no; Data was acquired via local or encrypted transport: no
-- Data from: cache

real	0m0.012s
user	0m0.003s
sys	0m0.007s
[jlquinn@tiamat seminar]$ time resolvectl query -i wlp4s0 -t aaaa sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com
sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com: resolve call failed: Name 'sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com' does not have any RR of the requested type

real	0m0.014s
user	0m0.003s
sys	0m0.007s

It looks like you're right about an upstream DNS not returning at all for ipv6 queries.  Here are the 2 commands in the failing env:

[jlquinn@tiamat seminar]$ time resolvectl query -t aaaa sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com
sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com: resolve call failed: All attempts to contact name servers or networks failed

real	0m41.799s
user	0m0.003s
sys	0m0.008s

[jlquinn@tiamat ~]$ time resolvectl query -4 sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com
sasvpn.raleigh.ibm.com: 129.42.49.10           -- link: wlp4s0

-- Information acquired via protocol DNS in 665us.
-- Data is authenticated: no; Data was acquired via local or encrypted transport: no
-- Data from: cache

real	0m0.011s
user	0m0.002s
sys	0m0.006s
So I guess there's another brokeness we have to prepare resolved for: that servers reply to A lookups but don't respond at all to AAAA lookups. Hmpf.
Is there a way for me to disable AAAA queries to work around the broken server?

For anyone else that encounters a similar situation, I was able to work around it by forcing a static DNS of 8.8.8.8 (bypassing the router and cable provider) on my wifi interface.

I'm happy to continue to provide debugging info as needed.

my temporary solution is to bypass systemd-resolved by edit `/etc/nsswitch.conf`, only let it to manage resolve.conf:
```
hosts:      mymachines files myhostname dns
#hosts:      mymachines resolve [!UNAVAIL=return] files myhostname dns
```

Please report this issue to the vendor of the router. DNS server should always respond to a query. It may respond with FORMERR, REFUSED or NOTIMPL, but it should respond. Dropping all AAAA queries is error on the side of vendor and should be fixed there. All other fixes are just workarounds. I would suggest offering other DNS server from such router, for example 8.8.8.8 of Google.

This is too fast for timeout. It just replied with no address, which is fine on any host not offering IPv6 addresses. This example is a different than the reported one. I think your example works fine.

I think it is wrong to print the response in red color. It is not an error if no such record exists:

```
$ resolvectl query -t txt localhost
localhost: resolve call failed: Name 'localhost' does not have any RR of the requested type
```
It did not fail. It got correct response there is no such record on that name. That should be more clear.
Hi is there any plans to fix this issue?

Same issue with a netcomm nf18mesh router, fc35 and/or fc36.

> rpm -q systemd
> systemd-250.8-1.fc36.x86_64


The router gets bored with answering AAAA queries. It'll work for a "while" after being rebooted but gets bored and stops. Might be related to the dhcp lease renewal time but I'm not sure, haven't bother investigating that.  

My workaround was to stop it from advertising itself and rely on the ISP's upstream dns server which works but screwed up what I had working for local single label name resolution.

While the _correct_ solution would be to have the router vendors fix their s**t that seems unlikely to me. Therefore resolved should be more robust against misbehaving servers and a plan to _make it so_ would be goodness.

barfo.

`SD_RESOLVED_NO_TXT` doesn't seem to make sense anymore because services are now resolved even when their TXT RRs are never received. It's probably an unintentional side effect.

Given that it's already on its way to the stable branch (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/35689) it would have been great to mention it somewhere since it changes the meaning of the resolved public API.
